newsitem.title: USA: U.S. donates $12.6 million for E. Africa refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. donates $12.6 million for E. Africa refugees.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was donating another $12.6 million to the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in response to an appeal for the Great Lakes area of East Africa.

State Department spokesman John Dinger said much of the aid would go toward finding, caring for and repatriating Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire.
The Great Lakes area also includes Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania and Uganda.

The United States has criticised Congo President Laurent Kabila for indifference to the fate of refugees after his forces began an uprising in eastern Zaire last October which led to the overthrow this month of President Mobutu Sese Seko.

The new donation raises the U.S. contribution to this year's U.N. appeal to $25.6 million, Dinger said. The United States says it has contributed more than $1 billion in humanitarian assistance to the Great Lakes region since 1993.
